summary.title: Avoid Building a Distributed Monolith
summary.one_liner: Learn why many service-oriented systems degenerate into tightly coupled distributed monoliths, and the practices (service modeling, integration, team organization) that keep services loosely coupled and cohesive.
takeaways: A distributed monolith is a system split into distributed parts that remain tightly coupled.
In such systems, changes to one service often force changes across several others, making deploys slow and risky.
Good service architectures aim to be loosely coupled and highly cohesive.
The talk covers three areas: modeling services, integration techniques, and organization structure.
The idea of small independent services predates microservices, under the name SOA.
summary.summary: This is a conference talk by Felipe Assis (speaker deck slides) given at the 1st Microservices Meetup in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, in July 2016. It argues that many SOA implementations have degenerated into distributed monoliths, where decomposed services are still tightly coupled and changes require coordinated updates across the system. The talk states the goal as a loosely coupled, highly cohesive service architecture and outlines three topics: how to model services, integration techniques, and organization structure. The page text is a brief abstract only, so specific techniques are not described here.
